title: Four guardrails keep model-written slides safe to ship
subtitle: The one place a model draws shapes, and how each slide it touches is contained

items.heading: Layout reuse budget
items.text: Each template layout is used at most twice; slides over budget are redrawn as diagrams by model-written code.

items.heading: Static gate
items.text: The code is the model's only spatial output. Static checks reject disallowed imports before anything runs.

items.heading: Contained changes
items.text: Every other slide is restored byte for byte; the reworked slide gets the standard checks and a vision review.

items.heading: Template fallback
items.text: A slide the code cannot get right keeps its template layout, so the deck always ships.

items.label: Bottom line
items.text: A model never breaks a deck: the worst case is a slide in its original layout.

notes: Model-written code is the one exception to deterministic assembly. Four guardrails bound it: a reuse budget decides when it runs, a static gate decides what may run, containment limits what it can change, and a fallback guarantees the deck still ships.
